name: High-cardinality time series
summary: A steady flood of timestamped points from many sources, each tagged with labels, that you query by time range and aggregate.
body: Metrics, sensor readings and market ticks arrive as timestamped values, mostly in time order, and are rarely changed afterwards. Each series is named by its labels (host, region, device, symbol), and every distinct combination of label values is a separate series. Cardinality is the number of those series. A label like a user ID or a container ID can turn thousands of series into millions, and many systems slow down or run out of memory long before they run out of disk.

A system built for this partitions data by time, compresses each series well (timestamps and values change slowly), drops or downsamples old data on a schedule, and can answer “average per minute over the last day, per host” without reading raw points one by one. To tell whether one handles your load, test with your real number of series rather than your number of points, and look at what happens to memory and query speed as series churn, for example when every deploy creates new pod names.
